newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Ports of Auck sees benefits from hubbing.
newsitem.headline: Ports of Auck sees benefits from hubbing.

text.p: Ports of Auckland chairman Sir Richard Carter said on Tuesday the increase in hubbing from the port should insulate Auckland from the effects of any economic downturn.

"Current New Zealand economic forecasts are mixed, with concerns about a downturn in the short term. However, the growth that has been achieved as a result of the increase in hubbing should continue to insulate Auckland from the full effects of any general decline," he said at the release of the company's full year profit results.
"With world class facilities as a result of our recent investment programme, we are poised to make excellent progress in the year ahead."
Hubbing describes a strategy whereby one shipping line bases all its operations at one port.
Ports of Auckland reported a year profit of NZ$39.4 million, which was down from $58.8 million a year ago due to two large one off items in 1995/96.
When the effect of one-off items was taken out, the after tax surplus was $37.6 million, compared to $39.3 million the previous year.
The company declared a fully imputed special dividend of 30 cents per share, bringing the total to 48 cps.
Carter said the special dividend meant the total distributed to shareholders in the 1996/97 financial year would be $63.6 million fully imputed.
He said the major future commitment for Ports of Auckland was the extension of the Ferguson terminal, which would cost about $120 million.
